title: Optional Binding with guard let

content.intro: This lesson focuses on optional binding with guard let and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Guard clauses”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Reusable functions and precise data models reduce duplication. Handling missing data and failures explicitly makes later application code safer to change.

content_blocks.title: Reasoning About Optionals
content_blocks.alt_text: The flow starts with an optional value, checks whether it exists, safely binds it and uses the resulting non-optional value.
content_blocks.caption: An optional is a value that may be present or absent.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** For guard clauses, identify the contract, the valid inputs, and the failure or boundary case. Write the smallest reusable Swift example that makes those decisions visible.

**Work through the lesson.** Represent absence with optionals and operation failures with errors; choose the right recovery path. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Scope of unwrapped values
items.text: An optional explicitly represents a value that may be absent. Check and bind it before using the wrapped value; avoid forced unwraps unless an invariant is proven.

items.title: Validating function inputs
items.text: A function names a unit of behavior with typed inputs and a return type. Clear argument labels describe call-site intent and make APIs easier to read.
